Korop Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Korop became part of the Russian Empire in 1667 and was, in the late 18th century, the center of the region's tanning industry, employing mostly Jewish workers, who also owned more than half the town's 119 trade enterprises; the population grew from 218 in 1862 to over a thousand by 1920. The community withstood pogroms in November 1917, 1918 (by Austro-German troops), and October-November 1919 (by Denikin's forces). The last Jew of Korop was killed on April 11, 1942.
